title: Steve 'Dr. Death' Williams: Sooner Guard Turned Pro Wrestling Star
question: Which former Oklahoma football player became pro wrestler Dr. Death?
answer: Steve Williams, a Sooner guard and four-time All-American heavyweight wrestler from 1979 to 1982, became the pro wrestling star known as Dr. Death. He entered the National Wrestling Hall of Fame in 2007 and the WWE Hall of Fame in 2021.
summary: Steve Williams played guard for Barry Switzer's Sooners and wrestled at OU, then became pro wrestling's Dr. Death, a star in Japan and Hall of Fame inductee.
body: Not every Sooner who made a name after football stayed in football. Steve Williams, a Colorado native from Lakewood, arrived at Oklahoma as an athlete who could do two things at once: block for Barry Switzer's offense and wrestle at heavyweight for the Sooners.

On the mat he was a four-time All-American, according to the National Wrestling Hall of Fame. His NCAA heavyweight finishes climbed from sixth to fifth to third and, in his final season of 1982, to second place, where he lost the title match to future Olympic medalist Bruce Baumgartner.

On the field he played for Oklahoma teams that won two Big Eight championships and went to five bowl games, three of them the Orange Bowl. He started at guard in 1982 and earned All-Big Eight honors that season.

Professional wrestling became his second career. Billed as Dr. Death, a nickname that traces back to a hockey goalie mask he wore in a junior high match, he worked for Mid-South, the UWF, All Japan, WCW and WWE. He was especially famous in Japan, where he won the Triple Crown Heavyweight Championship and teamed with Terry Gordy in All Japan's tag tournaments.

The recognition came later. Williams was inducted into the National Wrestling Hall of Fame as a professional wrestling inductee in 2007, and the WWE Hall of Fame Legacy Wing honored him after his death in December 2009 at age 49. For OU fans, he is a reminder of how many roads a Sooners uniform can lead down.
